overview.text: The Long-nosed Snake is a shy, harmless burrowing snake of the south-western United States and northern Mexico, named for its long, slightly upturned snout.

identification.text: Black and red saddles on a yellow or cream background - a little like a coral snake - with cream spots inside the black saddles. It has a long, slightly upturned snout.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-western USA (California and Idaho east to Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas) and northern Mexico.

behaviour.text: Active at night and spends most of its time buried underground.

diet.text: Lizards, amphibians and sometimes smaller snakes; rarely rodents.

reproduction.text: Lays 4 to 9 eggs in early summer, which hatch in late summer or early autumn.

recognise.text: Black saddles with cream speckles, between red patches.
